title: SLA-anchored observability scan and contextual alert matrix
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Customers with strict SLAs (latency and cost envelopes) need a proactive, low-cost way to detect drifting signal that will impact promised SLOs before pager noise spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight observability scan that anchors metric baselines to declared SLA windows and surfaces a contextual alert matrix that recommends remediation owners and severity. What changed at a glance: 1) a periodic 'SLA scan' job that computes per-route SLA deltas for latency, tail-latency, and token-cost drift (bucketed by prompt shape), 2) an alert matrix UI component (Dashboard: 'SLA Anchors') which shows prioritized cells with suggested owners and an auto-suppression TTL heuristic, 3) query and metric pipeline optimizations to run the scan cheaply across tenants (incremental rollups + single-pass aggregation), 4) a small set of instrumentation additions to token-phase timing spans so the scan can attribute per-token cost shifts to model/kernel phases, 5) a safety fallback policy that automatically lowers alert noise by auto-squelching alerts with <10 invocations in the detection window. Implementation notes: - SLA scan: implemented as a scheduled worker in observability/scan that reads per-route SLA definitions from the config service and computes three delta metrics: sla_latency_delta, sla_cost_delta, sla_tail_delta. Deltas are computed with exponential windowing so short spikes don't dominate. - Aggregation: added a new incremental rollup path in metrics/rollup that emits compact summaries keyed by (tenant, route, prompt_shape_bucket, model_variant). We reuse the existing reservoir histograms to approximate tails. - Token-phase timing: lightweight span tags added in runtime/trace_instrumentation to record phase durations (encode: token_gen_phase_ms, kv_cache_phase_ms, kernel_exec_phase_ms). Tags are categorical and low-cardinality. - UI: Dashboard tile 'SLA Anchors' added under observability/dashboards with matrix cells that link to per-route timeline, suggested owner, and a quick-run synthetic probe button. - Alerting: A new alert type sla-anchor-critical with tuned thresholds and a noise gate middleware that auto-suppresses churning cells. Backwards compatibility: Configs default to disabled for tenants without explicit SLA entries. Rollout plan: feature flag rollout over 2 weeks: 1) internal telemetry-only (week 1) 2) opt-in for customers via console (week 2) 3) default-on for tenants with SLAs (week 3, contingent on telemetry sanity). Checklist: - [x] Worker implementation and unit tests - [x] Rollup path and performance tests - [x] Low-cardinality span tags added and validated - [x] Dashboard and linking - [x] Alert policy and noise gate - [x] Documentation (console help + runbook) Testing and performance: Benchmarked the scan (10k routes across synthetic tenants) and confirmed the incremental rollups add ~0.8% CPU and <1% additional ingestion bytes by leveraging histogram compression. Synthetic probe generator was used to validate owner suggestions by correlating recent deploy tags and kernel-version changes. Rollback plan: Feature flag to turn off scan + a TTL to delete generated synthetic alerts. Related: ENG-3420 (SLA alert rationalization), ENG-3499 (token-phase minimal spans), SUP-7812 (customer reported early-warning requirement).
commits: 3 commits: a) add sla scan worker and rollup path; b) add token-phase span tags and tests; c) dashboard tile and alert policy wiring
review_comments: Diego Morales: Can you confirm retention implications for the new rollups? If we keep 30d rollups for all tenants this could grow; suggest tenant scoping.
Author (Aisha): We scoped rollups to tenants with SLA entries only and emit a compact 1KB summary per route per epoch; added note in deploy/feature_flags to ensure default-off for non-SLA tenants.
Priya Patel: The auto-suppression TTL seems aggressive for low-volume routes; suggest increase from 10m to 30m and add a decay-based re-alert window.
Author (Aisha): Agreed; bumped TTL to 30m and added exponential backoff for re-alerts in alerts/policies/sla_anchor_policy.yaml.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good. One nit: prefer reservoir seed determinism in test_sla_scan to avoid flaky tails.
release_notes: Add SLA-anchored observability scan and SLA Anchors dashboard: provides early detection of latency and cost drift tied to SLAs, plus an alert matrix with owner suggestions and noise gating. Disabled by default for tenants without SLA entries.
notes_for_oncall: If alerts begin firing en masse after rollout, flip feature flag sla_anchor_flag to off and run the synthetic_probe/generator local run to reconcile which routes caused highest variance. The scan writes compact rollups to metrics.rollup.sla_* metrics; monitor cardinality if retention policies are changed.
user_impact: Low: dashboards and alerts gated behind SLA entries and feature flag. Instrumentation adds low-cardinality span tags only.
